claims.support: Summarizes the topic of vulnerable employment differences globally.

claims.text: A look at the global divide in formal job security, comparing high-vulnerability economies like Chad and India against the low-vulnerability rates of Gulf nations and the USA.
claims.support: Chad (90.2%), India (71.6%), Saudi Arabia (1.7%), Qatar (0.5%), UAE (1.5%), Kuwait (2.4%), and USA (3.8%) match the World Bank dataset.

claims.text: In Chad, 90.2% of workers lack formal job security. In Saudi Arabia, it is 1.7%.
claims.support: Chad value is 90.224285798179% (display: 90.2%) and Saudi Arabia value is 1.66172984324461% (display: 1.7%).

claims.text: This counts contributing family workers and own-account workers as a percentage of total employment.
claims.support: Matches the evidence definition: Vulnerable employment is contributing family workers and own-account workers as a percentage of total employment.

claims.text: India has 71.6% of its workforce in these roles. That is 42 times the level in Saudi Arabia.
claims.support: India value is 71.583962506186% (display: 71.6%). Saudi Arabia value is 1.66172984324461% (display: 1.7%).

claims.text: China has 33.4% and Brazil has 26.1%. Both have more formal job security than India.
claims.support: China value is 33.3992901433807% (display: 33.4%), Brazil value is 26.0849820869874% (display: 26.1%), and India is 71.6%.

claims.text: The lowest rates? Qatar at 0.5%, the UAE at 1.5%, and Kuwait at 2.4%.
claims.support: Qatar value is 0.455955577569801% (display: 0.5%, rank 184), UAE value is 1.5011293226179% (display: 1.5%, rank 182), Kuwait value is 2.40281042159704% (display: 2.4%, rank 180).

claims.text: The USA sits at 3.8%. A tiny fraction of the vulnerable employment seen in India.
claims.support: United States value is 3.80976956797991% (display: 3.8%), India value is 71.6%.
